title: Gideon and the Letters
premise: Rosalind Galloway, a ghostwriter who abandoned his own name and voice after a betrayal twenty years ago, is hired to write the memoirs of Julian Voss—the rival who stole both his manuscript and the woman he loved. To survive a family reunion that demands he arrive with a partner, Rosalind recruits Maren Okafor, a warm, perceptive archivist who has her own reasons for pretending. As their fake relationship deepens and Julian's memoir forces Rosalind to transcribe the lie that destroyed him, he must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the careful, invisible life he built—until Maren discovers his ghostwritten pages and confronts him with the self he's been hiding. In the end, Rosalind publishes a memoir under his own name, forgives himself, and chooses Maren not as an escape from invisibility but as the first person to whom he's ever been fully visible.
about_author: Ansel Ishikawa is the pen name of a former archival researcher who spent a decade cataloguing other people's letters before turning to fiction. They write quiet romances about people who mistake safety for happiness.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Margins
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Establishes Rosalind's meticulous, hidden life as a ghostwriter and his ritual of erasing himself from every page. When an offer arrives to ghostwrite Julian Voss's memoirs, his agent insists he can't refuse. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professionalism; the reader senses a wound beneath the routine.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Rosalind meets Julian for the first time in twenty years; Julian is charming, unrepentant, and claims not to remember the stolen manuscript. The contract is signed with shaking hands. Emotional beat: suppressed rage curdling into resolve—Rosalind tells himself this is just another job.

chapters.title: An Invitation in Small Caps
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The Galloway family reunion looms, complete with a cousin's wedding and a grandmother who asks pointed questions. Rosalind's sister threatens to set him up with 'someone awful' unless he brings a date. Emotional beat: comic panic masking loneliness; the fake-date scheme is born out of desperation.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: POV Maren. Introduce Maren Okafor at the city archive where she preserves dead people's correspondence. She notices Rosalind researching old publishing records and offers help; their banter is easy in a way that unsettles them both. Emotional beat: two careful people recognizing each other's caution.

chapters.title: A Reasonable Arrangement
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Rosalind proposes the fake date; Maren, needing a plus-one for her own ex's engagement party, counters with terms. They rehearse their story over bad coffee. Emotional beat: playful negotiation layered with mutual wariness—both are lying about how much they want this.

chapters.title: Reunion
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The family reunion begins; Maren performs flawlessly, charming even the skeptical grandmother. But a cousin mentions the novel young Rosalind once wrote, and Maren catches the flicker of pain. Emotional beat: warmth with hairline cracks—the performance works too well.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: POV Maren. During dessert, Rosalind defends Maren against a backhanded compliment with unexpected ferocity, then kisses her cheek on instinct. Alone afterward, they admit the line has blurred. Emotional beat: vertigo—the fake thing feels truer than anything either has chosen deliberately.

chapters.title: Sessions with a Stranger
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Memoir interviews with Julian begin; Julian narrates the theft of 2004 as a misunderstanding, casting himself as the victim of a bitter collaborator. Rosalind types it all verbatim, hating his own hands. Emotional beat: quiet corrosion—loyalty to truth vs. the safety of silence.

chapters.title: What Maren Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Maren. Maren's chapter: her archive work, her ex, and why she agreed to pretend—she's spent years being someone's convenient option. She starts keeping a private folder of things Rosalind says offhand. Emotional beat: tenderness sharpened by fear of wanting more than the arrangement allows.

chapters.title: The Second Draft of Him
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Writing Julian's memoir at night, Rosalind finds his own prose bleeding into the ghostwriting—sentences too honest, too much his own voice. He deletes them, then saves one paragraph in a hidden file. Emotional beat: identity resurfacing like a scar under water.

chapters.title: Rain on the Fire Escape
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Trapped by a storm after a book event, they share wine and half-truths on Maren's fire escape. Rosalind almost tells her about Julian; instead he tells her about the novel, omitting the theft. Emotional beat: intimacy achieved through partial confession—closer, and guiltier.

chapters.title: The Grandmother's Letters
chapters.summary: POV Maren. Maren helps Rosalind's grandmother digitize old family letters and recognizes in them the same self-erasure Rosalind practices. The grandmother, sharp-eyed, tells Maren: 'He used to sign his name like he meant it.' Emotional beat: generational echo; love expressed as diagnosis.

chapters.title: Deadline Pressure
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Julian's publisher moves up the memoir deadline; simultaneously, Julian hints he knows Rosalind is 'the Galloway boy' from the old workshop days. Is it a threat or a test? Emotional beat: tightening vise—professional and personal timelines colliding.

chapters.title: The Paragraph
chapters.summary: POV Maren. Working late at Rosalind's apartment, Maren finds the hidden file: the deleted paragraph, written in a voice nothing like the ghostwriter's—and referencing events only the betrayed party could know. She says nothing, but everything shifts. Emotional beat: the ache of loving someone who is hiding in plain sight.

chapters.title: Loyalty, Illustrated
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Julian offers Rosalind co-authorship and public credit—a gilded trap that would bind him to the false version forever. Tempted by legitimacy at last, Rosalind nearly signs. Emotional beat: the devil's bargain made seductive; loyalty to his old dream vs. loyalty to truth.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Stacks
chapters.summary: POV Maren. Maren confronts Rosalind in the archive with the paragraph and what she's pieced together about Julian. She isn't angry about the fake dating—she's furious that he'd let Julian author his life twice. Emotional beat: climax of the emotional throughline; being seen as both wound and gift.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Small Steps
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Rosalind walks the city all night, revisiting the sites of his old life, finally admitting the person he most needs to forgive is himself—for hiding, for staying silent, for mistaking survival for living. Emotional beat: dark night of the soul turning toward dawn.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: POV alternating. At the memoir's launch event, Julian reads the falsified account aloud. Rosalind stands during Q&A and publicly tells the true story of the stolen manuscript, surrendering anonymity and career in one breath. Emotional beat: climax—truth spoken at maximum cost, hands steady for the first time.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Fallout: industry blacklisting, Julian's threats, but also an unexpected groundswell—readers and old colleagues who remember the original novel. Rosalind writes a statement in his own name and means every word. Emotional beat: grief and liberation arriving together.

chapters.title: His Own Name
chapters.summary: POV Maren. Maren watches Rosalind submit his own memoir—not revenge, but reclamation—to a small press. She waits to see if he'll reach for her now that the pretense is gone. Emotional beat: held breath; love offered without the scaffolding of a role.

chapters.title: Signed Like He Meant It
chapters.summary: POV alternating. At the grandmother's birthday, Rosalind gives her a printed copy of his new first chapter, signed in full. Maren and Rosalind renegotiate their arrangement into something real, with no terms except honesty. Emotional beat: resolution—the fake becomes true by becoming chosen.

chapters.title: Letters, Unhidden
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind, epilogue. A year later: the memoir is published, modestly successful; Rosalind teaches a ghostwriting workshop where he tells students to keep one paragraph for themselves. Final image: a letter from Maren on his desk, beginning 'To Rosalind Galloway,' read aloud in his own voice. Emotional beat: peace—identity, memory, and love finally on the same page.
